title: Jesus, I Love Thy Charming Name
description: Jesus, I Love Thy Charming Name in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 512 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Jesus precious to them that believe”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-sus, I love thy charm-ing name; 'Tis mu-sic to my ear; Fain would I sound it out so loud That earth and heaven might hear.

lines: Jesus, I love thy charming name;
Fain would I sound it out so loud
That earth and heaven might hear.
Whate'er my noblest powers can wish
No light unto my eyes so dear,
Thy grace shall dwell upon my heart,
The noblest balm of all its wounds,
I'll speak the honors of thy name
And, dying, clasp thee in my arms,

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
